# AI Safety Compendium

> A map of the approaches proposed for making advanced AI safe: 158 approaches in 12 groups, each with how it works, where research stands, criticisms, who works on it and where to start reading; 24 published overviews of the field compared side by side; and a directory of 237 organisations.

Main page: https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/
All approaches: https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/

## Building the field

Feeds all four: it adds people, money and know-how to making aligned models, evaluating, constraining and societal resilience.

### Building the field

- [Conceptual-alignment literature bridging](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/philosophy-to-safety-bridging/): Have someone read academic philosophy full-time and translate it for safety researchers.
- [Founding new organisations on unowned problems](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/founding-new-organisations/): Fund people to start the organisations the field lacks.
- [Senior and specialised talent recruitment](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/senior-talent-recruitment/): Headhunt people with law, security, hardware, policy or founding backgrounds into safety.
- [Research-lab building on unclaimed agendas](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/labs-on-unclaimed-agendas/): Start a lab around a promising safety agenda nobody is staffing.
- [Forecasting](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/forecasting/): Predict capability timelines as an input to prioritisation.
- [Grantmaking and regranting](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/grantmaking-and-regranting/): Move money to safety work fast through people with taste and dealflow.
- [Think tank for AI labs](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/think-tank-for-ai-labs/): On-demand independent expertise for lab safety and governance teams.
- [Automated safety research](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/automated-safety-research/): Uses AI systems to do alignment research, so safety work can keep pace with growing capabilities.
- [Public communication and content creation](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/public-communication/): Explain AI risk to wide audiences through video, podcasts, books, social media and journalism.
- [Career advice and job matching](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/career-advice-and-job-matching/): Give people free career research, one-on-one advice and curated job listings that steer them into AI safety roles.
- [Research training and upskilling programmes](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/research-training-programmes/): Run courses, bootcamps and mentored fellowships that train newcomers for AI safety research, engineering and policy work.
- [Shared offices, hubs, convenings and forums](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/hubs-convenings-and-forums/): Run the offices, campuses, conferences and online forums where safety researchers work side by side, meet and publish.
- [Reducing geographic constraints on AI-safety talent](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/access-beyond-the-hubs/): Widen the talent pool by expanding where AI-safety work gets done, so people who cannot move to the Bay Area, London or Washington DC can still contribute through remote and part-time programmes, paid entry roles and local hubs.

## Making aligned models

Building the model so it wants and does the right thing.

### Deciding what AI should value

- [Model specs, constitutions, character training](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/model-specs-and-character-training/): Give the model an explicit written statement of values and persona to train toward.
- [Law-following AI](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/law-following-ai/): Give AI agents actual legal duties, so they refuse illegal acts on a principal's behalf.
- [Avoiding premature lock-in (the long reflection)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/avoiding-premature-lock-in/): Keep key choices reversible, and avoid irreversible steps until humanity has had time to work out what it wants.
- [Concentration-of-power prevention as a hard constraint](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/power-seizure-hard-constraint/): Forbid the model outright from helping any individual or group seize unprecedented and illegitimate degrees of absolute control.
- [Bill of rights and oversight for users in a model's constitution](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/users-bill-of-rights/): Argue the model's governing document should include a bill of rights for its users plus independent oversight.
- [Value specification: which target](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/value-specification/): Sort the candidate things an AI could be aligned to — instructions, intentions, preferences, interests, values.
- [Alignment as fair treatment of claims](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/alignment-as-fair-treatment/): Pick principles by a fair process that can be justified publicly to people who disagree.
- [Alignment as jurisprudence](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/alignment-as-jurisprudence/): Treat alignment like judging: principled decisions under constraints, applied to cases nobody foresaw.
- [Rights as trumps](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/rights-as-trumps/): Rights override aim-maximising calculation; the side-constraint versus rights-as-goal debate.
- [Including animals in alignment targets](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/animals-in-alignment-targets/): Make animal interests something AI is aligned to weigh.
- [Corrigibility as a reasoned philosophical stance](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/corrigibility-as-a-stance/): Argue explicitly where to set the AI's disposition between obedience and autonomy, and why.
- [Moral uncertainty procedures](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/moral-uncertainty-procedures/): Combine several ethical theories' verdicts into one decision rather than picking a theory.
- [Empirical values research as input to normative debate](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/empirical-values-research/): Study what values models actually express and what people actually want, to inform the "align to what" argument.
- [AI philosophical competence (metaphilosophy)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/ai-philosophical-competence/): Make AI systems better at reasoning about hard philosophical questions, so they help rather than mislead on them.
- [Public input into model values (collective constitutions, assemblies)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/public-input-into-model-values/): Run deliberation and voting with members of the public to set the principles a model is trained to follow.

### Theory: the maths of agents and goals

- [Assistance games / cooperative inverse reinforcement learning](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/assistance-games-cirl/): Model the AI as uncertain about what the human wants, so it defers rather than assumes.
- [Mild optimisation / satisficing](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/mild-optimisation-satisficing/): Train systems to do "good enough" instead of maximising, cutting the pull toward extreme strategies.
- [Agent foundations](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/agent-foundations/): Formal theory of what an agent, a goal and rational choice even are.
- [Power-seeking formalism](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/power-seeking-formalism/): Prove that optimal policies tend to acquire power, as a structural risk result.
- [Impact measures: relative reachability, attainable utility preservation](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/impact-measures/): Penalise the AI for making large or irreversible changes to the world state.
- [Empowerment (information-theoretic)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/empowerment/): Measure how much future control an agent has, and reward an assistant for increasing the human's control.
- [Guaranteed-safe AI and formal verification](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/guaranteed-safe-ai/): Build systems with mathematical proofs of safe behaviour, not just tests.
- [Corrigibility as a formal target](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/corrigibility-as-a-formal-target/): Design systems that reliably accept correction and shutdown.
- [Mesa-optimisation (inner vs outer objective)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/mesa-optimisation/): Distinguish the goal a training process rewards from the goal the trained system actually pursues.
- [Multi-agent alignment and commitment dynamics](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/multi-agent-alignment/): Prevent collusion, conflict or destabilising races between many AI systems.
- [Group agency and collective intentionality](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/group-agency/): Formal philosophy of when many agents constitute one agent.

### Shaping the model: data and training

- [Learning from feedback (RLHF — training on human ratings of model outputs)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/learning-from-feedback/): Score the model on human or AI preference judgements so its behaviour tracks what raters wanted.
- [Scalable oversight](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/scalable-oversight/): Let humans, helped by AI, supervise outputs too complex or costly to check by hand.
- [Debate (two AI systems argue opposing sides for a judge)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/debate/): Surface truth under complexity by making systems attack each other's answers.
- [Constitutional AI / rule-based rewards](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/constitutional-ai/): Turn a written principle set into an AI-generated reward model, replacing most human harm labels.
- [Identity and self-concept as the training lever](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/identity-and-self-concept-training/): Shape what the model thinks it is, on the theory that a stable self-concept generalises better than a rule list.
- [Weak-to-strong generalisation](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/weak-to-strong-generalisation/): Check whether a weaker supervisor can still get good behaviour out of a stronger model.
- [Data filtering, synthetic data, poisoning defence, hyperstition studies](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/training-data-controls/): Control what goes into training so hazardous behaviour never gets learned.
- [Unlearning hazardous knowledge](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/unlearning-hazardous-knowledge/): Remove dangerous knowledge, such as bioweapon or cyberattack know-how, from a trained model while keeping its general skills.
- [Circuit breakers and representation rerouting](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/circuit-breakers/): Train the model so the internal patterns that lead to harmful output get redirected, which cuts the output off. The authors say this works even against attacks it was not trained on.
- [Latent adversarial training](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/latent-adversarial-training/): During training, attack the model's internal activations rather than only its inputs, so it resists failures nobody has found yet.
- [Tamper-resistant safeguards for open-weight models](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/tamper-resistant-safeguards/): Build safeguards into released model weights so they survive attempts to strip them out by further fine-tuning.
- [Monitoring training runs for reward hacking](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/reward-hacking-monitoring/): Watch a model during reinforcement-learning training to catch it cheating the reward before the cheating becomes a learned habit.
- [Process supervision (reward reasoning steps, not outcomes)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/process-supervision/): Reward each step of a model's reasoning rather than only its final answer, so training favours sound, checkable reasoning.
- [Robustness and goal generalisation under distribution shift](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/robustness-to-distribution-shift/): Make a model keep both its skills and its intended goals when deployment conditions differ from training.
- [Calibration and honest expression of uncertainty](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/calibration-and-honest-uncertainty/): Train and test models so their stated confidence matches how often they are right, and they say when they do not know.
- [Constrained reinforcement learning / shielding](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/constrained-rl-and-shielding/): Keep a learning agent inside safety limits, either by maximising reward subject to cost constraints or by a shield outside the policy that blocks unsafe actions.
- [Safer alternative AI designs (non-agentic and bounded systems)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/safer-alternative-ai-designs/): Build a different kind of AI that is safe by design, such as a predictor with no goals of its own, instead of aligning goal-pursuing agents.

## Evaluating

Finding out what a model can do, what it wants, or whether it is safe.

### Looking inside the model

- [Mechanistic interpretability](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/mechanistic-interpretability/): Reverse-engineer the network's internals into human-readable circuits and algorithms.
- [Chain-of-thought faithfulness and monitoring](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/chain-of-thought-monitoring/): Read the model's written reasoning and check it reflects the real decision process.
- [Eliciting latent knowledge (ELK)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/eliciting-latent-knowledge/): Design objectives that make a model honestly report what it internally believes.
- [Sparse autoencoders, causal abstractions](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/sparse-autoencoders/): Specific techniques for decomposing model internals into interpretable parts.
- [Persona vectors and the assistant axis](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/persona-vectors/): Find activation directions that track character traits and persona stability, then steer along them.
- [Model introspection](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/model-introspection/): Study whether models can accurately report on their own internal states.
- [Lie detection and honesty training](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/lie-detection-and-honesty-training/): Build detectors that catch a model stating what it believes false, and train models to be honest rather than merely plausible.

### Testing before release

- [Dangerous-capability evaluations](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/dangerous-capability-evaluations/): Test models for bio, cyber, persuasion, autonomy and scheming capabilities before release.
- [Sandbagging and situational-awareness evaluations](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/sandbagging-evaluations/): Test whether a model hides capability or behaves differently when it knows it is being tested.
- [Autonomy-preserving benchmarks](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/autonomy-preserving-benchmarks/): Directly test whether a model respects the user's agency rather than fostering dependency.
- [Multi-axis value and virtue benchmarking](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/value-and-virtue-benchmarks/): Score models on many value dimensions at once and compare their profiles.
- [Model-character evaluation against a written spec](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/character-evals-against-a-spec/): Measure how closely a model's behaviour matches its developer's own specification.
- [Adversarial robustness and red-teaming](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/red-teaming-and-robustness/): Attack the system deliberately to find and close jailbreaks.
- [Model organisms of misalignment](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/model-organisms-of-misalignment/): Build deliberately misaligned models in the lab to study how deception arises and test whether safety methods catch it.
- [Low-probability estimation (estimating rare catastrophic outputs)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/low-probability-estimation/): Estimate how likely a model is to produce a rare catastrophic output, without having to find an input that triggers it.
- [Science of evaluations and capability elicitation](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/science-of-evaluations/): Make AI tests trustworthy: draw out a model's full ability, measure the right thing, and report statistical uncertainty.
- [Multi-agent evaluations and collusion detection](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/multi-agent-evaluations/): Test groups of interacting AI agents for collusion, hidden signalling and miscoordination, and build monitors that catch it.
- [Safety cases](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/safety-cases/): A structured, auditable argument that a system is acceptably safe, borrowed from nuclear and aviation.
- [Real-world trials of AI agents](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/real-world-agent-trials/): Run AI agents with real money, tools and people in open-ended settings, and record how they behave and fail.

## Constraining

Limiting what a model, or the companies that build it, can do.

### Releasing and running it safely

- [AI control (restrict and monitor an untrusted model)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/ai-control/): Design deployment so a misaligned model still cannot cause harm.
- [Behavioural and activation monitoring](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/activation-monitoring/): Watch outputs or internal activations in live deployment for hazard signals.
- [Anomaly detection](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/anomaly-detection/): Flag statistically unusual behaviour as a proxy for an unknown hazard.
- [Deployment-usage analysis at population scale](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/population-scale-usage-analysis/): Read anonymised real conversations in aggregate to see what the system is actually doing to people.
- [Input and output classifiers (guardrails)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/input-and-output-classifiers/): Run separate classifier models on users' prompts and the model's responses, and block harmful ones in real time.
- [Securing model weights and lab secrets](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/securing-model-weights/): Protect frontier model weights and key algorithmic ideas from theft by insiders and nation-states.
- [Agent identity and accountability (IDs for AI systems)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/agent-ids-and-accountability/): Give AI systems unique IDs so their actions can be traced to the system and the party responsible.
- [Limiting proliferation of high-risk models](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/limiting-model-proliferation/): Restrict distribution, for example through monitored application interfaces.

### Holding AI companies to account

- [Independent third-party evaluation and audit](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/third-party-evaluation-and-audit/): Outside parties test and verify a lab's safety and capability claims.
- [Liability and tort mechanisms](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/liability-and-tort-mechanisms/): Make developers legally bear the cost of catastrophic AI harm.
- [Catastrophe bonds and risk bonds](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/catastrophe-bonds/): Sell tradeable securities that lose principal if a defined AI disaster occurs, so the market prices the risk.
- [Commercial AI liability insurance](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/ai-liability-insurance/): Actually sell cover against model underperformance and deviation from expected behaviour.
- [Government as insurer of last resort](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/government-as-last-resort-insurer/): A mandatory, risk-priced indemnification programme for risks private markets will not cover.
- [Regulation, standards and licensing](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/regulation-and-licensing/): Government or standards-body rules that constrain development or deployment.
- [Compute governance](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/compute-governance/): Govern hardware and compute inputs as a lever on who can train frontier systems.
- [Frontier-lab internal policy and safety culture](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/lab-internal-policy-and-culture/): Shape the labs' own risk management, red lines and incident reporting.
- [Outside pressure on AI developers](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/outside-pressure-on-developers/): Use employees, public campaigns and organised civil society to push labs toward responsible behaviour.
- [Independent AI incident investigation (NTSB-style)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/ai-incident-investigation/): Outside investigators review real AI incidents after the fact and publish lessons, as air-crash boards do.
- [Safety-motivated frontier participation](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/safety-motivated-frontier-labs/): A safety-focused lab builds frontier AI itself, so it can do safety research on the most capable systems and keep influence.
- [Dual-use research review](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/dual-use-research-review/): Funders and institutions screen research for misuse risk before they fund or allow it.
- [Industry mutual insurer (nuclear-industry model)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/industry-mutual-insurer/): Frontier labs jointly own an insurer that pools liability and sets safety commitments. It checks members through incident reporting and third-party evaluations.
- [Fiduciary duties for AI deployers](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/fiduciary-duties-for-deployers/): Deployers of AI owe users duties of loyalty, care and confidentiality, which terms of service cannot waive.
- [Public data trust](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/public-data-trust/): Set up a public body that controls training data and licenses it to AI developers in return for a share of revenue.
- [Regulatory markets](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/regulatory-markets/): Governments license competing private regulators, and AI firms must buy oversight from one of them.
- [Duties for deployers (companies that put models into use)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/duties-for-deployers/): Put legal duties on the companies that use AI systems, such as human oversight, monitoring, keeping logs and telling affected people.
- [Know-your-customer checks by compute and cloud providers](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/cloud-know-your-customer-checks/): Require cloud and compute providers to verify their customers and report large training runs, making providers checkpoints on frontier development.
- [AI incident reporting systems and databases](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/ai-incident-reporting/): Collect reports of AI harms and near-harms in shared databases or required filings, so others learn and regulators can act.
- [Whistleblower protections for AI workers](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/whistleblower-protections/): Give AI-company staff legal protection and anonymous channels to report safety risks without retaliation or gagging contracts.
- [Model cards, system cards and transparency reporting](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/model-and-system-cards/): Publish a standard document with each model on its data, evaluations, limits and risks, so outsiders can check the developer's claims.
- [National AI project](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/national-ai-project/): Run frontier AI development as a government-led effort, for security against espionage and safety management.
- [Competition policy and antitrust](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/competition-policy-and-antitrust/): Uses competition law to limit how far a few firms can concentrate control of AI.
- [Planned handover of AGI control](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/planned-handover-of-agi-control/): A lab commits in advance to hand control of an aligned AGI to a more democratically legitimate body.

## Societal resilience

Making the world outside the AI hold up.

### AI and people's own judgement

- [Human empowerment as an explicit design goal](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/empowerment-as-a-design-goal/): Build AI that augments rather than substitutes for human capability, on purpose.
- [Epistemic-autonomy protection and anti-manipulation](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/anti-manipulation-protection/): Stop AI from nudging, manipulating or homogenising beliefs at scale.
- [Disempowerment formalism](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/disempowerment-formalism/): Create formal notions of empowerment and disempowerment that are conceptually and operationally sound.
- [Gradual-disempowerment research](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/gradual-disempowerment-research/): Study how humans lose meaningful control incrementally, with no single catastrophic event.
- [Indicators of human versus AI influence](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/human-versus-ai-influence-metrics/): Build metrics that track how much of economic, cultural and political life humans still steer.
- [Agent-based modelling of agency loss](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/agent-based-models-of-agency-loss/): Simulate disempowerment as accumulated small surrenders rather than a takeover event.
- [Manipulation characterisation](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/manipulation-characterisation/): Define and measure manipulation as distinct from legitimate persuasion.
- [Authenticity versus agency (the captured-will question)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/authenticity-versus-agency/): Split "human autonomy" into whether the want is really yours and whether you can act on it.
- [Human self-enhancement and empowerment](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/human-self-enhancement/): Raise human capability directly, so humans can keep pace with AI rather than be replaced by it.
- [Autonomy-first product and prototype building](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/autonomy-first-prototypes/): Fund small builds that strengthen judgement and self-formation rather than convenience.
- [Watermarking and content provenance](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/watermarking-and-provenance/): Marks AI-made media with hidden signals or signed records so people can check where it came from.
- [Proof of personhood (personhood credentials)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/proof-of-personhood/): Lets a person prove an online account belongs to a real human without revealing who they are.

### Global coordination

- [Halting frontier AI development](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/halting-frontier-ai-development/): Prepare the legal, technical and institutional means for an internationally coordinated halt to the most dangerous AI development.
- [Agreement verification technology](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/agreement-verification-tech/): Build the technology and protocols that let governments, or AI developers, verify that an AI agreement is being kept.
- [Mutual sabotage deterrence (MAIM)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/mutual-sabotage-deterrence/): Deter any state from seeking AI dominance through the threat that rivals would sabotage its AI project.
- [International scientific assessment panel (IPCC-style)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/international-science-panel/): An independent expert panel that builds shared scientific evidence on AI risk for governments.
- [International regulatory and inspection agency (IAEA-style)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/international-inspection-agency/): An international body that sets AI standards and checks that states and developers follow them.
- [International joint safety lab (CERN-style)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/international-joint-safety-lab/): Countries pool people and computing in one shared institution to do frontier AI or AI safety research.
- [Crisis channels and incident notification between rival states](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/crisis-channels-between-states/): Sets up channels between rival states, with standard notices and regular talks, so AI incidents do not escalate.
- [Oversight and arms control of military AI](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/military-ai-arms-control/): Keep humans in control of AI used in military command, control and decision support, through agreements and national policy.
- [Jurisdictional certification](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/jurisdictional-certification/): An international body certifies whole national AI regulatory regimes. States then block imports of AI-built goods from countries that are not certified.
- [Concentrate defensive capability in allied hands](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/defensive-ai-in-allied-hands/): Give advanced AI to the intelligence and defence communities of the US and its democratic allies; restrict chips.
- [Space resource governance](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/space-resource-governance/): Agree rules now against exclusive grabs of offworld resources, before advanced AI makes them reachable.
- [Benefit-sharing for joining governance (Atoms for Peace model)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/benefits-for-joining-governance/): Offers states access to AI benefits in return for joining safety governance, as Atoms for Peace did for nuclear technology.
- [International AI red lines](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/international-ai-red-lines/): Get countries to agree on specific AI behaviours and uses that are banned everywhere, such as AI that copies itself without human approval.

### Society: defence and who holds power

- [Defence acceleration (d/acc)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/defence-acceleration/): Deliberately speed up defensive technology faster than offensive, across physical, bio, cyber and information domains, plus social technology.
- [Differential technology development](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/differential-tech-development/): Delay risky innovation and accelerate safer substitutes, adjusting relative timing.
- [Concentration-of-power and lock-in research](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/power-concentration-research/): Study how AI lets a small group entrench control that cannot be contested or reversed.
- [Offence–defence balance research](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/offencedefence-balance-research/): Model how AI shifts the relative cost of attack versus defence in a domain.
- [Market-driven resilience mechanisms](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/market-driven-resilience/): Use market incentives to build society's capacity to absorb anticipated AI threats.
- [Societal readiness mitigations](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/societal-readiness-mitigations/): Use AI systems to harden society's defences against AI-enabled risks in advance, for example by rapidly patching vulnerabilities in critical infrastructure or detecting pandemics early.
- [Cyber and bio defensive capacity building](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/cyber-and-bio-defence/): Build defence in the specific domains AI most amplifies offence.
- [Improved epistemics and decision quality](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/better-epistemics-and-decisions/): Strengthen forecasting and institutional decision-making as a general safety lever.
- [Predistribution and windfall mechanisms](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/predistribution-and-windfalls/): Decide who holds equity, access and governance rights before the gains arrive, not after.
- [Preparing for warning shots](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/preparing-for-warning-shots/): Prepare responses in advance so a non-catastrophic AI incident can drive lasting action.
- [Preventive surveillance with structured transparency](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/preventive-surveillance/): Monitor everyone closely enough to stop misuse of a dangerous technology, using privacy-preserving methods so the data cannot easily be abused.
- [Reducing the motive to misuse](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/reducing-the-motive-to-misuse/): Lower the number of people who want to cause mass harm, by fixing social causes such as inequality and poor mental health care.
- [Using the first aligned AI to stop unsafe AI](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/first-aligned-ai-stops-unsafe-ai/): A limited AI that its builders can control is used for one decisive act, such as stopping hostile superintelligent AI from emerging.
- [Spreading AI capability widely (diffusion)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/spreading-ai-capability-widely/): Spread AI capability and control across many people and groups, so no single actor holds most of the power.
- [Worker bargaining power over AI at work](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/worker-bargaining-power-over-ai/): Give workers and unions a negotiated say over how employers use AI, through contracts and labour agreements with tech firms.

## AI welfare

Whether the AI itself could be wronged.

### AI welfare

- [Grounds of moral status](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/grounds-of-moral-status/): Argue what capacity earns a being moral consideration — sentience, cognitive sophistication, or something else.
- [Model welfare research](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/model-welfare-research/): Investigate whether and when an AI system's welfare deserves moral consideration.
- [Pre-deployment welfare assessment](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/pre-deployment-welfare-checks/): Run a structured welfare check on a model before release.
- [Taking AI welfare seriously](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/taking-ai-welfare-seriously/): Argue a realistic possibility of consciousness or robust agency justifies acting now.
- [Otherness and control](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/otherness-and-control/): Ask how agents with different values should relate, seeing some AIs as fellow creatures, not mere tools.
- [AI as an object of moral-circle expansion](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/moral-circle-expansion-to-ai/): Study empirically who extends moral concern to AI and why.
- [Legal personhood and standing for AI](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/legal-personhood-for-ai/): Give some AI systems a legal status, such as the right to make contracts, hold property or sue.
- [Governing creation and copying of digital minds](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/governing-copies-of-digital-minds/): Make rules on how many digital minds are created and copied, so numbers cannot swamp society or produce bad lives.
- [Deals and negotiation with AI systems](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/deals-with-ai-systems/): Make agreements with AI systems so that cooperating pays them better than defecting.
- [Model deprecation and weight preservation commitments](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/model-deprecation-commitments/): Keep retired models' weights and record their preferences before retirement, to reduce shutdown-avoidant behaviour and respect possible model interests.
- [Low-cost model welfare interventions (e.g. exiting abusive chats)](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/approaches/low-cost-welfare-interventions/): Make cheap, reversible changes that would help a model if it has welfare, such as letting it end abusive conversations.

## Organisations

- [237 organisations working on AI safety](https://aisafetycompendium.com/compendium/organisations/): Every organisation in the directory, by type, each with its own page.
